roles.verdict: A, B and C are mathematically distinct functions of the same physical variable rho. A and C saturate; B grows as sqrt(rho) at high density and does not saturate. C is the same rational saturation template as A under the variable transform y=sqrt(rho/rho_crit), but not the same law in rho. The source presents BE -> von Neumann -> chain rule -> per-mode n(n+1) -> mode activation as the mediator, but supplies no single consistent derivation linking both BE exponents to one Gamma.

The corpus contains explicit CITES edges and a smaller set of explicit BUILDS_ON edges. Gamma is not normatively consistent across packages. Supersession is declared only as the 31942821 -> 31942800 companion upgrade to Scenario B+; full replacement is not declared. Seven DOI duplicate groups exist, all with divergent citations.bib.

A, B and C compete for the same Gamma role, not documented separate regimes. B and C carry different mediators (D_eff = rho/(rho+rho_crit) vs D_eff proportional to sqrt(rho/rho_crit)). No source shows a regime-bound transition making both valid in disjoint domains. The two BE exponents are also competing. 'Emergence' is parametric language, not a defined non-reducible property.

One intended unobserved target Gamma(rho) with three competing definitions, not three observables. Gamma is emergent in the theory but operates as a proxy when inferred. The public surface uses the square-root BE exponent for mu(g), not a direct Gamma measurement. This is a public-surface/DOI/code provenance conflict, not a physical falsification.

A -> B -> B+ cannot be defended as a pure maturation chain. KC1 is a proposed kill criterion, not an executed >=5sigma test. The square-root form is the theoretical consequence in 31941465 and 31878760, while 31942821 holds both linear and square-root notation. B -> B+ changes mode activation without a reported dataset or likelihood. The most direct discriminating base is galactic RAR/rotation curves (SPARC), not documented as pre-selected or actually used.

The public surface publishes B, B+ and the phenomenological rho/(rho+rho_crit) form simultaneously without selecting one. The public BE exponent is sqrt(g/a0), agreeing with code but conflicting with 31942821 metadata. The primary issue is public-surface and metadata consistency, not an established physical contradiction.
